newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Burma assures Bangladesh on refugee repatriation.
newsitem.headline: Burma assures Bangladesh on refugee repatriation.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday that she had received assurances from Rangoon that all Burmese refugees in Bangladesh would be repatriated by the end of this month.
"Myanmar (Burma) authorities have assured Bangladesh that all Rohingya refugees would be repatriated by March 31 this year," Hasina told parliament.
Hasina said 24,742 refugees were now in three camps in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar district, bordering Burma's western Arakan state.

"Myanmar has also assured that they would identify the reasons behind the massive Rohingya influx into Bangladesh and take steps to stop a recurrence of such incidents," she said in answer to questions from a ruling Awami League party legislator.
More than 250,000 Burmese Moslems, called Rohingyas, fled to southeastern Bangladesh in early 1992 from Burma's Moslem-majority Arakan province, complaining of military persecution.
Repatriation, supervised the the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, began in September that year following an agreement between Dhaka and Rangoon.
